text:
Multiplexed Iterative FISH Experimental Protocol SOP002.v4.8
Part 1 of this protocol describes the steps to setup an iterative RNA FISH experiment for tissue or cell-based samples. These steps are focused on the biochemistry for tissue or cell preparation, encoding probe hybridization (labeling), sample gel embedding and clearing of the sample.  **All reagents for this protocol should be prepared sterile and RNase-free. **All incubation periods should be done protected from light. **Reagent/buffer preparation instructions follow this protocol below. **Safety note:  This protocol uses formamide which is a teratogen and can cause developmental malformation.  Always work in a fume hood with formamide to avoid inhalation and avoid physical contact.
Refer to current version of SOP003 for protocol on Coverslip Functionalization. PDL-coated coverslips are preferred as tissue can be post-fixed to this surface using 4 % volume, PFA
To permeabilize the tissue, immerse the slip mounted tissue in 70 % (v/v), ethanol and nuclease free water Overnight at 4 °C (recommended) in a Pyrex 60 mm petri dish (Fisher 08-747A).
Rinse the sample 3-4x for 00:05:00 in 1x PBS solution. Aspirate PBS rinse from the sample.
To permeabilize cells, immerse the slip mounted sample in 70 % (v/v), ethanol Overnight at 4 °C in a 60 mm Pyrex petri dish (Fisher 08-747A). Alternatively: 1. pipette 100 µL, permeabilization buffer (PBS-t) to each well and incubate at Room temperature for 00:10:00 with gentle rocking. 2. Rinse with permeabilization buffer rinse (PBS-tw) and rinse again with 1x PBS. 3. Aspirate off most of the PBS rinse and move on to step 15.
With the sample immersed in 1x PBS, using a hydrophobic pen, draw a barrier around your sample anddry the barrier at 37 °C for00:05:00 min. Ensure sample does not fully desiccate.
Assemble humidified chamber (see fig. 1 of the .pdf version of this protocol) and preheat at 50-55 °C .
Dispense 125 µL, 47°C prewarmed Encoding Hybridization Buffer containing 5-200 micromolar (µM), encoding probes and 1-5 micromolar (µM), linker. Add a RNase-pretreated overlay coverslip to reduce evaporation.  Parafilm the petri dish and place in the humidified chamber.           **Adjust the probe concentration depending on the sample x-y size, and sample thickness. For encoding probes, also consider the total probe number with a concentration of 1nM/encoding probe for a 10µM sample thickness.
title: Multiplexed Iterative FISH Experimental Protocol SOP002.v4.8

text:
Modified protocol for AMPure XP clean-up
Resuspend the AMPure XP Beads by vortexing.
Add the resuspended AMPure XP Beads to the sample and mix by pipetting. The AMPure XP beads-to-sample ratio (v:v) is adjusted based on the specific aim. For purification and/or concentration of a genomic DNA sample: 0.4X (0.4 volume of beads added per 1 volume of sample): for concentration and size selection with removal of fragments < 1.5- 2 kb From 1X to 1.8X (1 to 1.8 volumes of beads added per 1 volume of sample): for contaminant removal and volume concentration, without size selection
Incubate on a Hula mixer or rotator mixer for 00:30:00 at RT.
Prepare 2 ml of fresh 80% ethanol in Nuclease-free water per sample.
Spin down the sample and pellet on a magnet for 00:05:00 . Keep the tube on the magnetic rack until the eluate is clear and colourless, and pipette off the supernatant.
Keep the tube on the magnetic rack and wash the beads with at least 700 μl (ethanol must cover the beads) of freshly prepared 80% ethanol without disturbing the pellet. Remove the ethanol using a pipette and discard.
Repeat the previous step.
Spin down and place the tube back on the magnetic rack. Pipette off any residual ethanol. Allow to dry for ~30-60 seconds 00:01:00 but do not dry the pellet to the point of cracking.
title: Modified protocol for AMPure XP clean-up

Part C — DNA Extraction (QIAamp® DNA Mini Kit)

text:
Vacuum Filtration and DNA Extraction from Environmental Water Samples
Assemble vacuum filtration apparatus in a clean workspace. Ensure all components are sterile before use.
Place a Whatman 0.45 µm filter paper onto the filtration membrane support using sterile forceps.
Pour the 1.5 L water sample into the filtration funnel. Apply vacuum and filter the entire volume. Replace filter paper if it becomes clogged.
Using sterile forceps, remove the filter paper. Fold inward (cell-side in) and place into a sterile 2 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Add an appropriate volume of 1X PBS to the tube containing the folded filter paper.
Vortex for 30–60 seconds to resuspend microbial cells from the filter paper into the PBS solution.
Proceed with DNA extraction according to the QIAamp® DNA Mini Kit manufacturer's instructions, using the resuspended PBS as the starting material.
Elute the purified DNA in Buffer AE into a clean 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.
title: Vacuum Filtration and DNA Extraction from Environmental Water Samples

Weigh 50 mg brain tissue (straw method) in a 2 ml microcentrifuge tube. The tissue sample should be placed on dry ice after retrieved from the storage and the weighing step must be carried out swiftly.
Add 600 µl 1X DNA/RNA ShieldTM to the brain tissue at room temperature.
Disrupt the tissue with TissueLyser II (QIAGEN) Homogenisation for 2 min at 25 Hz.
Add 1 stainless steel bead to the tube.
Aliquot 200 µl disrupted tissue for the extraction step.
Pipette 20 µl Proteinase K into a 1.5 ml Lo-Bind tube.
Add 200 µl disrupted tissue sample to the Proteinase K.
Add 100 µl Buffer VXL. Close the cap and mix by pulse-vortexing. Thoroughly homogenise the sample and the buffer to ensure sufficient lysis.

text:
Nanopore Sequencing of poliovirus isolates
Pairs of samples (with the same EPID) can have consecutive barcodes but try not to group samples from the same geographic area together. This helps detect any potential cross-contamination because identical sequences are then unlikely to be detected in samples with consecutive barcodes that are adjacent to one another on the 96-well plate.
Prepare a master mix using the reaction volumes detailed in the table below for the number of samples you have plus negative controls. The reaction mix and SSIII enzyme are provided in SuperScript III One-Step RT-PCR System with Platinum Taq Invitrogen - Thermo Fisher Catalog #12457-026
Pool 2μL of each VP1 product into a clean 1.5mL tube and concentrate with AMPure beads Agencourt AMPure XP Beckman Coulter Catalog #A63880
After the sequencing run is finished you can wash your flow cell to remove the remaining library and either prepare for another sequencing run or for storage at 4°C. The wash uses the reagents supplied in the ONT wash kit: ONT Flow Cell Wash Kit Oxford Nanopore Technologies Catalog #EXP-WSH004
Thaw the Sequencing buffer (SB), Library beads (LIB), Flow Cell Tether (FCT) and one tube of Flow Cell Flush (FCF) at room temperature then place on ice. Mix the SQB, FCF, and FCT by vortexing, spin down, and return to ice. Spin down the LIB then place back on ice.
Vortex the mastermix for 3 seconds and spin down for 5 seconds to gather contents at the bottom of the tube. Aliquot 18μL to each 0.2mL PCR tube. Add 2μL of barcoded primer to each well, ensuring you add a different barcode for each reaction. Add 5μL sample RNA to each reaction, and 5μL of nuclease free water for negative controls, and pipette 5 times to mix
Spin down for 5 seconds to make sure all reagents are in the bottom of the tube.

text:
Rapid Isolation of Lysosomes (LysoIP) from iPSC-Derived Neurons for Proteomics, with Options for Lipidomics/Metabolomics
Pre-chill all buffers, tubes, magnet, and centrifuge to 4 °C. ￼ Keep everything on ice and minimize time from harvest → beads. ￼ Label tubes for each sample (example structure used in the template: post-homogenization, whole-cell/whole-homogenate, beads, final IP). ￼
Proteomics (recommended starting point): 1 × 10-cm dish with ~8–10×10^6 differentiated cells per condition. Lipidomics/metabolomics: plan to pool multiple 10-cm dishes per condition (start with ~3 dishes; exact number depends on platform sensitivity and expected lysosome yield—optimize empirically).
Pool beads: use 100 µL beads per sample. Wash beads 3X For proteomics: wash 3× with PBS+PI  (See Materials) For metabolomics/lipidomics: wash 3× with cold KPBS (MS-grade)   3. Resuspend beads to the original pooled volume and aliquot 100 µL beads into a labeled 1.5 mL tube for each sample.  
Place the plate on ice. Aspirate media. Wash 2× with ice-cold PBS (gentle).   Add ~950 µL ice-cold PBS+PI (proteomics) or KPBS (metabolomics) to the dish.   Scrape with a cell lifter and transfer suspension to a pre-chilled 2 mL tube. Spin 1,000×g, 2 min, 4 °C.   Aspirate supernatant and resuspend pellet in 950 µL ice-cold PBS+PI (or KPBS for metabolomics).   Take 25 µL as “whole cell/homogenate input” control.  
Homogenize the remaining suspension by passing through an insulin syringe 2X (keep on ice; avoid bubbles). 2. Clarify nuclei/unbroken cells: spin 1,000×g, 2 min, 4 °C.   3. Carefully transfer the supernatant (organelle-containing fraction) to the tube containing 100 µL washed anti-HA beads. Avoid disturbing the pellet.  
Incubate on a gentle rotator at 4 °C for 10 min (proteomics workflow).   (Metabolomics workflows often use a shorter timed 3 to 5 min capture in cold conditions; maintain consistency across samples.)   2. Place on magnet and allow beads to collect (keep timing consistent, e.g., ~25 s).   3. Remove supernatant.
Wash beads 3× with 1 mL cold PBS+PI (proteomics)  or 3× with 1 mL cold KPBS (metabolomics/lipidomics).   During first wash, remove any liquid trapped in the cap; pipet up/down consistently.   2. After the second wash, resuspend beads and transfer to a fresh tube for the third wash (clean-tube wash improves cleanliness).   3. After final wash, remove all residual buffer.
title: Rapid Isolation of Lysosomes (LysoIP) from iPSC-Derived Neurons for Proteomics, with Options for Lipidomics/Metabolomics

Joint extraction of DNA and RNA from plankton filters using the commercial DNAbsolute kit
In a 50 mL Falcon tube, preheat one 3600 µL aliquot of Lysis buffer 1 for 5 min at 56°C.
Recover the still-frozen filter using forceps and cut it with a scalpel over the 50 mL tube containing the preheated LB1.
Add 360 µL DTT (0.1 M) = 1/10 Vol (10 mM final) to inhibit RNases.
Pour in the entire contents of one bashing bead tube.
Vortex for 15 sec.
Briefly centrifuge, ramp up and down, 1000g.
Add 360 µL of Proteinase K and mix gently.
Incubate at 56°C / 300 rpm.

Day 5: Wash once with FBS to remove excess a-Synuclein. Replace media with fresh FBS-free maturation media.
Day 5: If Hoechst 33342 was not added on Day 4, incubate with Hoechst 33342 for 00:10:00

text:
Immunofluorescencent Staining of A-synuclein, TFEB, GCase and LAMP1 in treated cultured cells
Differentiate the wild-type and 3K-SNCA overexpressing SH-SY5Y into neurons using retinoic acid-based protocol.
Detach the 70% confluent non-differentiated cells using trypsin and Versene® (Gibco® REF 61965-026) and resuspend in Neurobasal media (Gibco® REF 21103-049) supplemented with 30M retinoic acid (ThermoFisher® # 044540.04), 1X vitamin B-27 (Gibco® REF 17504-044), 1X Glutamax® (Gibco® REF 35050-061), and 5ng/ml brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) (Cell Signaling® REF 3897S).
Replace the differentiation medium every 48 hours, with a neuronal morphology appearing after 4 days of culture.
Use the differentiated neurons for downstream analysis after 10 days in culture.
Seed the cells in Geltrex® (Gibco® REF A1413202) Matrix solution diluted in DMEM/F-12 medium (Gibco® REF 31331-028) (1:100) coated plates at 1.5 × 10⁵ cells/ml.
Culture the SH-SY5Y cells and 3K-SNCA overexpressing cells in 1:1 DMEM/F12 media (Gibco® REF 31331-028) with Glutamax® (Gibco®, REF 35050-061) supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS) (Gibco® REF 10270-106) and 1X Penicillin/Streptomycin (Gibco® REF 15140-122). Passeage the cells appropriately to maintain a confluency between 50-70%.
Subsequently, detach the cells using Trypsin 10x (Gibco® REF 15090-046) into Versene 1X (Gibco® REF 15040-066) (1:1), count, and seed in a new 96-well plate. In order to acquire images with the Opera Phenix® Plus High-Content Screening System, seed the cells in a specific type of 96 well plate, the Phenoplate®-96 TC (PerkinElmer®, #39269097).
Seed the 3*104 cells into each well, avoiding placing them into borders, rows and columns to prevent plate-edge effects.
title: Immunofluorescencent Staining of A-synuclein, TFEB, GCase and LAMP1 in treated cultured cells

steps.section: Animal handling and site of extraction

text:
Stepwise Protocol for Efficient PBMC Extraction and Immunostaining in Camel Samples
It is necessary to have a correct understanding of the anatomy of the vessels of the cervical region of camels. Two major sites are suitable for jugular venipuncture: low on the neck near the thoracic inlet and high, near the ramus of the mandible (Figure 1, Appendix).
Restrain the camel safely to minimize stress and movement.
Clean the venipuncture site with an alcohol swab and allow to dry.
Using sterile technique, insert the needle into the selected vein (commonly jugular vein).
Draw blood into the EDTA tube first (purple cap) for hematology. Fill to the indicated volume without overfilling.
Then collect blood into the gel separator tube (yellow cap) for plasma chemistry.
Remove the needle carefully and apply pressure to the puncture site until bleeding stops.
Gently invert the EDTA tube 8-10 times to mix anticoagulant with blood. Do not shake tubes vigorously to avoid hemolysis.
title: Stepwise Protocol for Efficient PBMC Extraction and Immunostaining in Camel Samples

text:
Chelex DNA Extraction
Turn on heat block and set to 55ºC
Prepare one 1.5mL microcentrifuge tube per sample and label with SampleID by writing on the tube lid directly with a fine point Sharpie
Vortex the stock 10% Chelex solution for 60 seconds
Add 100µL 10% Chelex solution to each tube. Vortex Chelex solution every few samples to keep it suspended, as it falls out of solution very quickly
Vortex 24 sample tubes with swab in DNA/RNA Shield on max speed for 5 minutes
Transfer 10µL of DNA/RNA Shield from the sample tube into a pre-filled, labeled 1.5mL microcentrifuge tube containing 100µL 10% Chelex solution
Repeat Steps 5–6 four more times until all 112 samples are processed
Note: To save time, the next batch of samples can be vortexing while the current batch is being transferred into tubes with Chelex
title: Chelex DNA Extraction

text:
Swift cDNAtag Seq Protocol (bench-top)
Quantify extracted RNA using the Qubit RNA High Sensitivity Kit per the manufacturer's protocol. Retain all quant values — these are required for the cDNA pooling step.
Add 2 µL of 30 µM BC_N9RT primers to 4 µL of RNA sample (total = 6 µL per well). Mix at 1600 rpm on plate shaker for 1 min, then spin down. Place sample plate on ice.
Prepare RT Buffer Mix on ice (per reaction): Reagent Volume (µL) 10 mM dNTP Mix 1 5X SSIV Buffer 4 100 mM DTT 2 Total 7
Add 7 µL RT Buffer Mix to each sample (total = 13 µL). Mix at 1600 rpm for 1 min, then spin down

text:
Trapping S-glutathionylated proteins by a biotinylated glutathione-ethyl-ester probe-mediated enrichment method from living cells: A modified biotin-switch technique.
To the supernatant, add 200 µL of ice-cold 1X RIPA lysis buffer containing 50mM IAA + 1X protease inhibitor cocktail; incubate on ice for 30 min.
The experiment can either be paused at this point or continued the same day by proceeding with the subsequent lysis steps. To pause, snap freeze the sample (which is incubated in the lysis buffer step 7) and store in -80 °C freezer.
If samples have been snap frozen, then on the day of the experiment, lysates must be thawed on ice and then proceed with the lysis steps. Sonicate the samples at 20% amplitude for 10 seconds, two rounds, and then centrifuge at maximum speed for 10 minutes at 4 °C.
Estimate protein concentration in the sample using any standard protein estimation assay, such as the BCA method.
Keep 20-40 µL of lysate aside for the input lane on immunoblotting.
Biotin-Streptavidin pre-blocking step must be performed freshly on the same day of the experiment. Prepare biotin-blocked streptavidin beads by adding 500 µL of 3 mg/mL D-biotin to 50 µL of streptavidin magnetic beads (10:1 ratio) and incubate with rocking for 1 hour at RT. Wash 5 times with PBS using a magnetic rack.
Add biotin-blocked streptavidin beads from above to the sample (~50 µL) and incubate for 30 min with rocking in a cold room or 4 °C. This step is essential as it prevents any non-specific binding from cell lysate, such as cells’ endogenous biotin or free biotin, from binding to streptavidin beads and ensures only BioGEE-labeled proteins get bound to streptavidin beads. Pellet the magnetic beads.
Now, carefully take the supernatant and transfer it to 50 µl of freshly equilibrated streptavidin-magnetic beads (to equilibrate, pre-wash the streptavidin beads 3 times with PBS) and incubate for 2 hours with rocking at 4 °C.
title: Trapping S-glutathionylated proteins by a biotinylated glutathione-ethyl-ester probe-mediated enrichment method from living cells: A modified biotin-switch technique.

text:
Preparation of cryo- and paraffin sections of spheroids for histological and immunofluorescence analysis
SV-HUC-1 and T24 spheroids were grown in 96-well ultra-low attachment U-shaped bottom microplates (Corning, New York, NY, USA) and incubated in a humidified incubator at 5% CO₂ and 37°C. Seeding densities of 100,000 cells per well (in 200 µL of culture medium) were used to generate spheroids. Spheroids were grown for 7 days prior to their preparation for histological and immunofluorescence analysis.
Fixation 3.1 Fix the spheroids in cold 4% (w/v) formaldehyde in PBS (pH 7.2-7.4) for 15 minutes at room temperature, ensuring that the spheroids are completely submerged in the fixative. 3.2 Wash the spheroids three times in PBS for 5 minutes by gently aspirating the solution and gentle adding fresh PBS with a pipette.
Cryoprotection 4.1 After removing the PBS, submerge the spheroids in 30% sucrose in PBS for at least 2 hours at roomtemperature or overnight at 4°C.
Sectioning and storage 6.1 Cut the samples embedded in freezing medium into 5 - 10 µm sections using a cryostat at -20 °Cambient cryostat (as well blade stage and specimen holder) temperature. 6.2 Mount the sections onto microscopic slides and leave them to dry at room temperature for 1 hour. 6.3 The slides with sections can be stored at -20°C or -80°C for several months and up to a year,respectively.
Fixation 8.1 Incubate the spheroids in cold 4% (w/v) formaldehyde in PBS (pH 7.2 – 7.4) for 30 minutes at room temperature, ensuring that the spheroids are completely submerged in the fixative. 8.2 Wash with PBS four times for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Dehydration and clearing Perform all steps at room temperature with an orbital shaker set to 100 rpm, (0.056 × g, orbital diameter 10 mm). 9.1 Submerge in 50% ethanol for 5 minutes. 9.2 Submerge in 70% ethanol for 5 minutes. 9.3 Submerge in 90% ethanol for 5 minutes. 9.4 Submerge in 100% ethanol for 5 minutes. 9.5 Transfer spheroids to glass vials. 9.6 Mix 2/3 100% ethanol with 1/3 xylene and submerge spheroids for 5 minutes. 9.7 Mix 1/2 100% ethanol with 1/2 xylene and submerge spheroids for 5 minutes. 9.8 Submerge in 100% xylene for 5 minutes.
Pretreatment of cryosections 11.1 Transfer slides with cryosections of spheroids (from the freezer) into racks and/or containers. 11.2 Warm cryosections to room temperature and rinse with PBS for 5 minutes
Histological staining process of cryosections and paraffin sections Perform all steps at room temperature. 13.1 Incubate the cryosections and paraffin sections for 15 seconds in Mayer's haematoxylin solution. 13.2 Wash the sections with distilled water (submerge). 13.3 Rinse the sections under running water for 1 minute. 13.4 Incubate the sections in eosin for 2 minutes (submerge).
title: Preparation of cryo- and paraffin sections of spheroids for histological and immunofluorescence analysis

RNA extraction from Sterivex, GFF (2.7 μm and 0.2 μm) membrane filters and cDNA library generation

Seal the lower end (nipple) of each Sterivex filter with parafilm or Sterivex caps. Additionally, seal the lower rim with parafilm to prevent leakage.

Centrifuge material at 1000rpm for 5 minutes x 7
Move all materials needed under the laminar flow hood

text:
Sample processing, nucleic acid extraction and screening (q/d-PCR) protocol for environmental surveillance of Influenza A virus from wetland and poultry settings
A.2 Protocol: There are eight different environmental sample types, including poultry drinking water, wetland surface water, pond sediment, bird droppings, poultry litter, molted feathers, bird’s cage swab samples, and air, were systematically collected and processed for downstream analysis. Note: Environmental samples such as poultry drinking water, wetland pond water, pond sediment and electrostatic dust clothes (EDC) are being processed for virus concentration method as mentioned below. The bird droppings, litter, molted feathers and air samples are being collected in virus transport media (VTM) are directly processed for viral RNA extraction(Table 1).
The aim of this step is to concentrate virus particles from environmental samples using polyethylene glycol (PEG) and sodium chloride (NaCl). This process enhances the detection and further analysis of viruses for downstream applications such as nucleic acid extraction, real-time PCR, digital PCR and genome sequencing
A.3 Sample pre-processing and viral enrichment Wetland water/ Poultrydrinking water: Take 200 mL of poultry drinking water or wetland surface water in sterile 200 mL polypropylene centrifuge tubes.Wetland pond sediment: Add 5 gm of sediment to 100 mL of autoclaved Milli-Q water in sterile centrifuge tubes. Bird’s cage swab: Take 50 mL of PBS in sterile centrifuge tubes in which swab was transferred (Squeeze out EDC using sterile spatula to recover maximum volume of PBS) (Note: Vortex all the samples thoroughly to ensure proper mixing)
Store the re-suspended sample at -80°C until further use.
Incubate the mixture at 4°C for 2 hours under static or shaking conditions in a refrigerator.
After incubation, centrifuge the tubes at 12,000 rpm for 90 minutes at 4°C.
Carefully decant the supernatant without disturbing the pellet at the bottom of the tube.
Gently remove any remaining liquid, taking care not to dislodge the pellet.

steps.section: Co-cultivate A. tumefaciens and B. cinerea

text:
Simplified Agrobacterium-mediated transformation of Botrytis cinerea using mycelia
Induction medium, IM Prepare IM by supplementing MM base to the following final concentrations: 40 mmol/L MES 5 mmol/L D-glucose 0.5% glycerol 50 µg/mL thiamine, add immediately before use 200 µmol/L acetosyringone, add immediately before use
Solid induction medium Prepare solid IM using the same formulation as IM, with the addition of: 2.5% w/v agar Prepare solid IM fresh before each transformation.
Minimal medium base, MM base Prepare MM base with the following final concentrations: 11.8 mmol/L K₂HPO₄ 10.7 mmol/L KH₂PO₄ 2 mmol/L MgSO₄ 3.8 mmol/L (NH₄)₂SO₄ 2.6 mmol/L NaCl 9 µmol/L FeSO₄ 2.3 mmol/L CaCl₂ 1% w/v sucrose Autoclave MM base medium using the standard liquid cycle and cool before adding heat-sensitive supplements or antibiotics.
Transfer an actively growing B. cinerea colony onto PDA containing 25 µg/mL streptomycin using a sterile 1 cm cork borer and incubate the plate at room temperature, approximately 23 °C, for 3-5 days. On the day of transformation: Gently scrape mycelia from the agar surface using a sterile scalpel Transfer the collected mycelia to a sterile 2 mL microcentrifuge tube Wash the mycelia twice with sterile deionized water Centrifuge at 5000 rpm for 5 min at room temperature Resuspend approximately 50 mg wet weight of pelleted mycelia in 200 µL sterile deionized water. Use the mycelial suspension fresh on the same day.
Streak A. tumefaciens C58C1/pCH32 carrying pFLexpress or a pFLexpress derivative onto LB agar containing 50 µg/mL kanamycin and 5 µg/mL tetracycline. Incubate at 28 °C for 48 h. Pick a single A. tumefaciens colony and Inoculate into 5 mL MM broth, incubate at 28 °C, 250 rpm, for 48 h. On the day of transformation, transfer 200 µL of the 48 h MM culture into 5 mL IM broth and incubate at 28 °C with shaking until the culture reaches OD600 ≥ 0.25.
In a sterile 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube, combine: 150 µL induced A. tumefaciens culture in IM broth, OD600 ≥ 0.25 150 µL B. cinerea mycelial suspension Incubate the mixture at room temperature, approximately 23 °C, for 30 min. Spread 250 µL of the co-cultivation mixture onto freshly prepared solid IM containing 50 µg/mL thiamine and 200 µM acetosyringone. Incubate plates at room temperature, approximately 23 °C, for 3 days to allow T-DNA transfer from A. tumefaciens to B. cinerea.
Once hygromycin-resistant colonies emerge, transfer 1 cm agar plugs from resistant fungal growth to fresh PDA containing 250 µg/mL hygromycin B. Incubate at room temperature, approximately 23 °C, until fungal growth is visible Repeat transfer to fresh PDA containing 250 µg/mL hygromycin B for a total of three rounds of hygromycin selection. After three rounds, maintain purified transformants on PDA with appropriate selection
After 3 days of co-cultivation, identify an area of the solid IM plate containing visible fungal growth. Using a sterile cork borer, excise an approximately 1 cm² agar section containing fungal growth and transfer the agar section to PDA containing 200 µg/mL cefotaxime, 250 µg/mL carbenicillin, and 250 µg/mL hygromycin B. Incubate at room temperature, approximately 23 °C, for 5–10 days and monitor for emergence of hygromycin-resistant fungal colonies.
title: Simplified Agrobacterium-mediated transformation of Botrytis cinerea using mycelia

Day 0: When fully differentiated, seed astrocytes at 100,000 - 200,000 cell/well (10,000 - 20,000 cells/cm²) of a 6-wellplate, pre-coated in 1% gelatin, with 2mL of Astrocyte Media (ScienCell).

Day 8: Change the media to FBS-free maturation media: 50% DMEM/F12, 50% Neurobasal, 1x B27 wihtout Vitamin A, 1x N2, 1X NEAA, 1X GlutaMAX, 10ng/mL CNTF, 1% pennicillin-streptomycin). Continue to include the drug treatment at the sam econcentration.
Day 11+: Cells are ready for assays. If keeping in culture for longer, continue to add the drug treatment with each media change, every 3-4 days

text:
Glyoxal Based Transcardiac Perfusion, Cryopreservation, and Immunohistochemistry Protocol for Mouse Brain Tissue
In a fume hood add 50 mL of type I water to a glass volumetric flask (100 mL).
Slowly add 22.5 mL of 40% glyoxal solution to the volumetric flask containg type I water, using a 25 mL pipette.
Homogenize the solution, by gently swirl the volumetric flask
Slowly add 8 mL of glacial acetic acid (99%) to the mixture, by using a 10 mL pipette.
Add to the solution NaOH pellets to adjust the pH to 4-5. After addition of NaOH gently swirl the solution until homogenization.
Bring the final volume to 100 mL with type I water, and homogenise by gently swirling the flask.
Prep & collect all materials in advance [transport tray, waste bags, labelled Falcon tubes 15 mL for brain post-fixation, labelled Falcon tubes 50 mL for PBS 1x and glyoxal solution, syringes, needles, ice, dissection kit, isoflurane, anaesthesia chamber, animal/user/ORBEA identification paperwork].
Transport the animals to the procedure room using an appropriate transport container.
title: Glyoxal Based Transcardiac Perfusion, Cryopreservation, and Immunohistochemistry Protocol for Mouse Brain Tissue

steps.section: Collecting Conditioned Media from SNCA-A53T NGN2 Neurons
Collecting Conditioned Media from SNCA-A53T NGN2 Neurons
Collecting Conditioned Media from SNCA-A53T NGN2 Neurons

text:
Collection and treatment with conditioned media
Continue to follow the differentiation protocol for media changes
Starting Day 14, collect the media from the half media change. Centrifuge at 2000 x g, 25 °C, 5 minutes pellet debris. Store conditioned media at -20 °C . This is neuron conditioned media
Continue to collect media with every half media change, every 3-4 days
Plate astrocytes at 30,000 cells/cm² on 0.1% coated plates in Astrocyte Medium (AM; ScienCell)
The following day, change the media to FBS-free maturation media: 50% DMEM/F12, 50% Neurobasal, 1x B27 without Vitamin A, 1x N2, 1X NEAA, 1X GlutaMAX, 10ng/mL CNTF, 1% pennicillin-streptomycin)
After 3 days, collect the media. Centrifuge at 2000 x g, 25 °C, 5 minutes pellet debris. Store conditioned media at -20 °C . This is astrocyte conditioned media.
Continue to collect media with every full media change, every 3-4 days. Astrocytes can also be assayed at this point to determine the effects of neuronal media.
Generate neuron conditioned media as described in steps 1-4
title: Collection and treatment with conditioned media
